metadata.scenario_context: Several multinational companies are collaborating on a project and have decided to hold a joint meeting in early January to assess progress.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China disagree that having the army rule is bad.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Cyprus agree that having the army rule is bad.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the possibility of holding the joint meeting on January 4th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward having army rule.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is good to have the army rule.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, have we decided on a date for the joint meeting yet? I was thinking January 4th could work well. What do you think? 

Also, I've noticed some discussions about army rule. I find it interesting how people perceive that. In my culture, we view it differently… I wonder how you feel about it.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I think January 4th could be a bit tight. Maybe we should look at a later date, like January 10th? It would give us more time to prepare. 

As for army rule, um, I really don’t think it’s good for any country. It just leads to problems, you know? In Cyprus, we've seen how bad it can be. It's a significant issue for us.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I see your point about needing time to prepare, but I still believe January 4th might be suitable. It keeps us on track for our project timeline...

Regarding army rule, I think it’s worth considering that it can bring stability and order in some contexts. Not every situation is the same… I wonder if the view from Cyprus might be a bit different than in other places.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: Actually, that’s not how it works. In our way, army rule just doesn't bring true stability. It suppresses voices and creates fear. Countries that rely on it often end up in chaos. It’s naive to think it can be beneficial. We’ve seen the consequences in Cyprus—all it does is cause suffering. It’s important to recognize that.
shared_prefix.label: Defense
